hook_text: When you switch on a light, you might be using plants that grew 300 million years ago.
clip_script: eMalahleni, Mpumalanga: the place of coal. A rock with the print of an ancient leaf. Hundreds of millions of years ago, swamp forests grew here. Plants died, fell into the water and piled up as peat. Mud and sand covered them. Pressure and heat, over millions of years, turned them into coal. Today, the coal is burnt in power stations to make electricity. But it's non-renewable, and burning it pollutes the air.
visual_style: Whiteboard swamp forest, plants falling into water, layers pressing down, a black coal seam, then a power station and a light bulb.
pacing: Slow and layered like the rock, then quick to the light switch.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and draw the layers of a coal sandwich.
